reason: The cited evidence does not directly support the key premises. E1 describes tribolayer formation in a different Ni-based alloy, not CoCrFeNi with carbon. E2 and E3 discuss carbide types and WC-reinforced composites, but provide no evidence that adding 0.2–0.5 wt% carbon to CoCrFeNi yields uniformly dispersed nanoscale Cr-rich carbides, nor that such carbides catalyze a self-lubricating tribolayer across the full temperature range. The premises are largely unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: Adding 0.2–0.5 wt% carbon to CoCrFeNi and heat treating at 800 °C yields nanoscale Cr-rich carbide precipitates
These precipitates will be uniformly dispersed
The precipitates will catalyze formation of a protective, self-lubricating tribolayer
This tribolayer maintains low friction and wear from RT to 800 °C
The carbides will not coarsen or cause embrittlement under these conditions
